title: Supremum commutes with adding a constant
statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite, nonempty type, let $f : \iota \to \bbn$ be a function, and let $c \in \bbn$ be a natural number. Then
\[
  \sup_{i \in \iota} \bigl(f(i) + c\bigr) \;=\; \Bigl(\sup_{i \in \iota} f(i)\Bigr) + c.
\]
replaced:
For any finite nonempty type $\iota$, function $f : \iota \to \mathbb{N}$, and constant
$c \in \mathbb{N}$,
\[
  \sup_{i \in \iota} (f(i) + c) \;=\; \left(\sup_{i \in \iota} f(i)\right) + c.
\]
This is a technical arithmetic lemma used in complexity calculations.
